title: An ALMA Search for Substructure, Fragmentation, and Hidden Protostars in Starless Cores in Chamaeleon I
question: Do starless cores in Chamaeleon I show substructure/fragmentation or hide protostars undetected by Spitzer+Herschel, and is the protostar census complete?

what.value: LABOCA core catalog, positions, masses, peak densities

evidence.quote: the phase center of our ALMA observations (taken directly from the core positions given by Belloche et al.)
list the YSO from (cite: winston2012:chami) associated with each detected source
list the associated protostar from the (cite: dunham2013:luminosities) compilation of protostars detected by *Spitzer*

what.value: Peak intensities of Perseus candidate FHSCs

evidence.quote: Peak Flux Densities of Candidate First Hydrostatic Cores in Perseus

what.value: OH5 dust opacity kappa=0.23 cm2/g at 106 GHz

evidence.quote: We adopt the dust opacities of (cite: ossenkopf1994:oh5) appropriate for thin ice mantles

recipe.method: imfit elliptical Gaussian fits to primary-beam-corrected images; 5 sigma detection threshold
M = 100 d^2 S/(B(T_D) kappa); n = 3M/(4 pi mu m_H r_eff^3)
key_parameters: T_D = 10 K, d = 150 pc, kappa=0.23 cm2/g, mu=2.37
assumptions: gas-to-dust ratio 100, OH5 dust, optically thin isothermal dust

recipe.goal: Classify evolutionary status via multiwavelength associations and SEDs
recipe.method: cross-match ALMA detections with LABOCA, Herschel, Spitzer catalogs; SEDs to assign protostellar/starless/disk
scale peak intensities of four Perseus faint protostars to 150 pc and 106 GHz with I ∝ nu^(2+beta), 0<=beta<=2, compare to rms
assumptions: same dust temperatures in Chamaeleon I as in Perseus; emission compact/unresolved

recipe.goal: Synthetic ALMA observations of simulated cores and BE spheres
recipe.method: convert column density to 106 GHz maps with BE-derived T(N) and OH5 opacity; simobserve/simanalyze with alma.cycle1.3.cfg, 72 s, 6 GHz; clean to 0.3 mJy
key_parameters: cloud background A_V=35.6 added; pixel 20 AU; distance 150 pc

recipe.goal: Predict expected detections and Poisson probability
recipe.method: Detections > N_total (n_Detectable/n_Limit)^-0.5 with tau ∝ n^-0.5, then Poisson probability of zero
assumptions: continuous star formation; free-fall evolution; simulations applicable

evidence.quote: We detect a total of 24 106 GHz continuum sources to 5$\sigma$ or greater significance in 19 different target fields
leaving us with 56 starless cores, none of which are detected by our ALMA continuum observations

answer_key.quantity: misclassification rate of protostellar cores as starless

evidence.quote: the rate at which protostellar cores in Chamaeleon I have been misclassified as starless cores is $<$1/56, or $<$ 2%
gives total masses ranging from 0.012 M$_\odot$ to 1.7 M$_\odot$
The C04 simulation is detected over the last 8200 yr of the starless stage, when the central number density exceeds $8.9 \times 10^{7}$ cm$^{-3}$.
The C4 simulation is detected over the last 11000 yr of the starless stage, when the central number density exceeds $3.3 \times 10^{7}$ cm$^{-3}$.
the total number of expected detections is reduced from at least three to at least two
the probability of detecting zero cores when two detections are expected is 13.5%

not_stated_but_needed: robust/weighting, deconvolver, clean threshold and masks for the real data
flux calibrator and flux scale uncertainty, CASA version
primary beam correction and mosaic details
how the 5-sigma limit and rms per field were measured
orion simulation snapshots and initial setup files (not released)
how orientation averaging gave 'at least two' detections
score_reason: Data public and photometric results are simple, but imaging settings and simulation inputs are unstated.
rediscovery_reason: Public data and numeric detections/flux densities with a simple mass formula; synthetic part is harder.
